title: Semi-supervised learning (scikit-learn documentation)
use: Graph propagation/spreading and confidence-controlled pseudo-labeling; not an external source of trial records.

title: Nested versus non-nested cross-validation (scikit-learn)
use: Separate model-selection scores from estimates of generalization.

title: Clustering (scikit-learn documentation)
use: Compare geometric assumptions and inductive extensions for multiple cluster families.

title: Zhu, Ghahramani, Lafferty (2003), Semi-Supervised Learning Using Gaussian Fields and Harmonic Functions
use: Harmonic graph inference with known-label boundary conditions.

title: Zhou et al. (2004), Learning with Local and Global Consistency
use: Normalized graph diffusion; custom multi-output implementation.

title: Waegeman et al. (2014), On the Bayes-Optimality of F-Measure Maximizers
use: Decision-theoretic motivation for sample-F1 decoder. Our simple enumeration uses independent marginal probabilities, not the full GFM joint-distribution algorithm.

title: Read et al. (2009), Classifier Chains for Multi-label Classification
use: Evaluate label-dependence models with cross-fitted chain features.

title: RDKit Getting Started
use: Morgan fingerprints and numerical descriptors computed only from supplied SMILES.

title: Joachims (1999), Transductive Inference for Text Classification using Support Vector Machines
use: Motivation for low-density semi-supervised margins. Our alternating pseudo-label procedure is a heuristic, not an implementation of the exact TSVM optimization algorithm.

title: Huang et al., Correcting Sample Selection Bias by Unlabeled Data
use: Kernel mean matching weights, estimated only against original masked training features.

title: On Mixup Regularization
use: Motivation for synthetic interpolation; evaluated with classical logistic/SVM learners only.

title: Nystroem kernel approximation, scikit-learn
use: Classical finite kernel features for comparing squared hinge, logistic and squared losses.

title: Cortes, Mohri, Rostamizadeh: Algorithms for Learning Kernels Based on Centered Alignment
use: Search-gap audit and classical methods; no additional trial data.

title: Zhou and Li: Tri-Training
use: Search-gap audit and classical methods; no additional trial data.

title: SVC documentation
use: Search-gap audit and classical methods; no additional trial data.

title: Sugiyama, Krauledat, Müller (2007): Covariate Shift Adaptation by Importance Weighted Cross Validation
use: Motivation for target-aware model selection. Estimated, clipped weights and label-dependent sampling here do not establish an unbiased target-risk guarantee.

title: Breiman: Bagging Predictors
use: Motivation for averaging fixed bootstrap runs; no best-seed selection.

title: scikit-learn: StackingClassifier
use: Meta-learners must learn from out-of-fold component predictions; custom implementation uses embedding-grouped inner folds.

title: Dembczynski et al.: An Exact Algorithm for F-Measure Maximization
use: Exact expected sample-F1 decoding under an estimated label-pattern distribution; estimated probabilities need not be correct.

title: Blum and Mitchell: Combining Labeled and Unlabeled Data with Co-Training
use: Motivation for separate embedding/metadata views exchanging pseudo-labels. Our quota, agreement, weighting and cluster safeguards are adaptations; the original assumptions are not established here.

title: scikit-learn: NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis
use: Gold-only per-reason linear metric learning, combined with original distances in an SVM kernel.

title: scikit-learn: Probability calibration
use: OOF score calibration motivates reliability estimates for pseudo-label weighting. Our target distribution is shifted, so calibrated target-domain accuracy is not guaranteed.

title: Segata and Blanzieri: Fast and Scalable Local Kernel Machines
use: Motivation for local SVM specialists; our overlapping weighted experts and global blending are a separate implementation adapted to this small dataset.

title: Lipton et al. (2018): Detecting and Correcting for Label Shift with Black Box Predictors
use: Motivates estimating changed reason frequencies from unlabeled examples. Our binary soft-confusion estimator uses ridge shrinkage; the stable conditional-distribution assumption may fail here.

title: Belkin et al. (2006): Manifold Regularization
use: Motivates Laplacian SVM penalties. Our experiment uses a finite 192-component Nystroem kernel approximation and fold-local graph fitting.
